The purpose is to build a reliable overview of Mechatronics Engineering before moving into specialized courses. Focus on systems, requirements, models, materials, measurement, design constraints, safety, efficiency, and sustainability.

Begin with the vocabulary and the central problem the field tries to solve. Then connect each principle to a simple academic or professional example. Avoid memorizing isolated sentences; organize ideas into causes, evidence, processes, and outcomes.

In this field, useful study habits mirror professional reasoning: define the question clearly, gather relevant evidence, choose an appropriate method, check assumptions, interpret the result, and state limitations. Important skills include quantitative reasoning, technical drawing or modeling, measurement, troubleshooting, documentation, and safe design practice. Prioritize core principles, units and assumptions, worked calculations, design trade-offs, and interpretation of diagrams or technical cases. Practice short explanations in your own words, then test yourself with a scenario that requires application rather than recall.

- Can I explain how the major ideas relate to one another?
